who: People working in a second language
takeaways: People are told how long they can be inactive before they lose data, unless the data is kept for more than 20 hours of inactivity.
It is Level AAA. 2.2.1 is about warning and extending a limit as it runs out. 2.2.6 is about telling people the limit up front, so they can plan breaks.
People who need to rest, check documents or ask for help can do so safely when they know how long they have.
Designers decide where and how the limit is stated, such as at the start of a flow. The simplest way to meet it is often to keep data for more than 20 hours.
failures: A booking form that clears after 15 minutes of inactivity, with no mention of it
A basket that empties after an hour, and nobody was told
The limit only mentioned in the terms of service
check: Ask developers how long each flow keeps data while people are inactive.
For every limit under 20 hours, find where people are told about it before they start.
Read the message as a first-time visitor and check it gives a clear length of time.

quiz.question: An insurance quote form loses answers after 30 minutes of inactivity. What is the best way to meet 2.2.6?
options: Save drafts for more than 20 hours, or state at the start: “Your answers are kept for 30 minutes if you are inactive”
Show “Your session has timed out” after the answers are lost
Add a Save button at the end of the form
quiz.why: Telling people after the loss is too late, and a Save button at the end does not protect a half-filled form. Either keep the data for over 20 hours, or tell people the limit before they begin.

spec: List each flow, how long it keeps data while inactive, and whether it is over 20 hours.
For limits under 20 hours, place and word the notice, such as on the first step and near the start button.
Say whether autosave or drafts could remove the need for a notice.
review: If someone stops to find a document, how long until they lose their work?
Where do we tell them that, and will they see it before starting?
Could we just keep the data longer instead?
tradeoff: Keeping data longer raises privacy and storage questions, while a notice adds words to a busy screen. Prefer saving drafts for over 20 hours where it is safe, and where it is not, use one short line at the start of the flow.
system: Add an inactivity notice to the flow start template that shows the time limit, and default form components to saving drafts.
pitch: Telling people how long they have costs one sentence. Not telling them costs a lost form and a lost customer.
